findings.title: Flex.Item grow={1} is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`
findings.body: The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `<Flex.Item grow={1}>` renders `flex-grow:1; flex-shrink:1; flex-basis:auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With basis `auto`, the description and feature list start at their content width. The sibling `Metadata` block (line 265; it sets no flex properties and so shrinks by default) is then squeezed when the description is long. Before, the description started at 0 and only took the leftover space. `Flex.Item` accepts `flex`, so `<Flex.Item flex="1">` keeps the old layout.

findings.title: New title truncation and environment lookup are not covered
findings.body: The comment format now goes through `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`, `_truncate_title` (50 characters) and `get_environment_info` (src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:577-606). The tests only use short titles and one dev/prod environment. Nothing covers a title over 50 characters, or the `except Exception` fallback in `get_environment_info` that returns an empty string. The GitLab tests have the same gap, because both integrations share this code. A test with a long title and one where `get_recommended_event` raises would pin the behaviour.

findings.title: Age/timestamp exclusivity tests miss the falsy and neither-present cases
findings.body: The serializer checks exclusivity with truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` in src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:52 and :58). `test_mixed_fields` only sends `age=1` with a nonzero timestamp. A report with `age=0` and a `timestamp`, which the validators accept, is untested. So is a report with neither field, which `required=False` also accepts. Add cases that assert the intended behaviour, or tighten the validators to check `is not None` and add a test for that.

findings.title: max_segment_id=None here is never exercised
findings.body: `delete_matched_rows` is patched in this test (line 82), so the `None` row is only passed to a mock. The null handling lives in `_make_recording_filenames` (src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py:89). Changing the fixture value does not test it. Add or point to a test of `_make_recording_filenames`/`delete_matched_rows` with `max_segment_id=None`. Note also that `run_bulk_replay_delete_job` and the `delete_replays_script_async` paths in src/sentry/replays/tasks.py (lines 91 and 251) still type `max_segment_id: int`.

findings.title: New 'Project not found' branch has no test
findings.body: The project now comes from `replayRecord.project_id`, and a new error state renders when that project is not in the projects store. There is no spec in `static/app/views/replays/detail/ai/`. A test for this branch would also cover the switch away from the `project` query param.

findings.title: Tests use seconds for both breadcrumb and error timestamps, which hides a likely unit mismatch in the merge order
findings.body: `gen_request_data` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153-155) compares each error's `timestamp` with each recording event's top-level `timestamp`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore and is in epoch seconds. Replay recording events are rrweb events, and I believe their `timestamp` is in epoch milliseconds. `event_parser.py:387` treats a payload timestamp as an int, but I did not find a conversion to seconds. If the units differ, every error timestamp (~1.7e9) is smaller than every event timestamp (~1.7e12). All errors would then be emitted before all breadcrumbs, and the summary would get a wrong timeline with no error. The new tests cannot catch this. `test_get_with_error` uses `now.timestamp()` for the segment event (line 254 in the sibling test, line 188 in the first) and `now.timestamp() - 1` for the error. `test_get_request_data` uses 1.0–3.0 for both. Use a realistic millisecond timestamp for the recording events, and assert the position of the error line relative to the breadcrumb line. Confirm the unit in the producer or the frontend, then fix the comparison in the endpoint if they differ.

findings.title: The `division by zero` assertion does not show that `message` is populated
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` fills `title` from `data['title']` and `message` from `data['message']`. For an event stored with an `exception`, the title is probably `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`. The line is built as `'{title}: {message}'`, so both substring asserts pass from the title alone. They would pass even if `message` were empty. If `message` matters, assert on the full formatted line. Otherwise drop the second assert so it does not suggest coverage it lacks.

contracts.action: AI summary tab resolves the project from replayRecord.project_id instead of the ?project= query param, and shows a new 'Project not found' alert
contracts.equivalent_path: Other replay detail code that resolves projects via useProjectFromId({project_id}) against the projects store.
contracts.before_after: Before: the project id came from the URL query. If it was missing, the project was undefined, the query stayed disabled and the tab showed a loading spinner forever. After: the id comes from the replay record, and when the id is set but the project is not in the store an explicit error alert is shown (lines 90-96). The query is enabled only when the replay id, the project slug and the feature flag are all present (lines 71-75).
contracts.visible_effect: The AI summary loads without a project query param. If the project is not in the user's projects store, the user sees 'Project not found. Unable to load AI summary.'
contracts.failure_mode: API failure shows the existing 'Failed to load AI summary' alert (lines 106-112). If replayRecord has not loaded, project_id is undefined, the query is disabled and the loading spinner shows until the record arrives. No silent failure found.

contracts.action: Tests for the new TableWidgetVisualization (header names, custom columns, number formatting, custom renderers)
contracts.equivalent_path: GridEditable consumers using renderHeadCell/renderBodyCell with getFieldRenderer.
contracts.before_after: The spec relies on GridEditable's data-test-id 'grid-head-cell', on renderDefaultHeadCell rendering the name inside a single wrapper (so children[0].textContent is the name), and on getFieldRenderer using meta.fields/units. The 'sentry-fixture/tabularColumns' alias maps to tests/js/fixtures. I read all of these and they match what the spec asserts.

contracts.action: Replay summarize endpoint merges nodestore error events into the breadcrumb log sent to Seer, and `enable_error_context=false` skips this
contracts.before_after: Before: only breadcrumbs went to Seer. After: error lines are interleaved by comparing error timestamp (seconds, from nodestore) with rrweb event timestamp.
contracts.visible_effect: The AI replay summary includes or omits error context, and the error position in the timeline depends on the timestamp comparison.
contracts.failure_mode: fetch_error_details swallows all exceptions and returns [], so a nodestore failure silently drops error context. The tests do not cover that path.
contracts.open_question: Are rrweb event timestamps in the segment data in milliseconds, while nodestore error timestamps are in seconds?

summary:
**Batch 3 of 4, retry.** This part is mostly mechanical test updates and `styled('div')` to `Flex` swaps. I checked the specs against the sources they test and they match: the single-`yAxis` `Visualize` API, the browser-collector validation messages, the PR-comment templates (including the blank-line counts for GitHub and GitLab), and the new default of `off` for `autofix_automation_tuning`. The one behavioural difference is in `integrationLayout.tsx`: `Flex.Item grow={1}` is not the same as the removed `flex: 1`, so the Metadata block can be squeezed when the description is long. The rest are small test-coverage gaps: truncation and environment lookup in the PR comment, falsy `age`/`timestamp` values in the collector, the `None` row in the delete test (which only reaches a mock), and the new 'Project not found' state. The PR body says 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', but this part also touches dashboards, explore, integrations, grouping and migrations.

**Batch 4 of 4.** The detector owner tests, delayed-workflow signature updates and logs top-events test look consistent with the code I read. In the replay summarize tests, both the breadcrumb and error timestamps are in seconds. If rrweb event timestamps are really in milliseconds, the real merge order would be wrong and these tests would not show it. I raised that as a medium-confidence finding. I did not read the other part's source to settle the unit.
